notes: Windows revision 3. Fixes the 'Runtime error (at 9:1397): Type Mismatch' and the follow-on 'setup did not work' report on clean Windows Server 2025. r2 had replaced the Pascal named constant HKLM with an explicit $80000002 integer root, but Inno Pascal treats a plain untyped hex const as a signed 32-bit Int32, so $80000002 evaluates to -2147483646, which Inno's RegKeyExists engine does not recognise as HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE - the service-key branch still misfired. r3 removes the Pascal-side registry read entirely: [Registry] writes SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CertMate before CurStepChanged fires, so by ssPostInstall that key is present on every successful install; post-install validation now checks only the on-disk deliverables (CertMateService.exe, export_pfx.py, updater.py) via FileExists. No named HKEY constant, no typed const, no hex literal - no type-ambiguity surface remains in the [Code] section. r3 also keeps the self-contained .NET 8 host + PFX/updater tools + docs + service registration + pre/post checks. Upstream v2.55.1 application tree + embedded Python are NOT in this payload (skipped network step on the dev build host); this revision ships the self-contained .NET host + PFX/updater tools + docs + service registration + pre/post checks only. A full end-to-end build (with upstream source + Python 3.12 embeddable staged under {app}\app and {app}\python) requires running Build-Release.ps1 on a networked build host.
